ARCS kitOrganism 70week-plan

Week Plan

Lay out a plan week by week: what will be true by the end of each week, how it cascades from executive to surgical, where the kairos forks sit and what must be true at each, and how best, base and worst play out, with keep and kill switches, on-ramps, off-ramps, opportunity cost and stop-losses on one color-coded sparkline.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1Tab sparklineEach week's tab carries three branch ends and the stop-loss; a week not drafted is one flat dashed line; steel until an ROI value is setorange, green, red, dimmed
2Week stripBest, base, worst as lanes D1 to D7: orange until the stop-loss (opportunity cost), a gold stop mark, then steel until an ROI value is set, green or red by its sign after; kairos forks as gold dashed lines; on-ramps cyan, off-ramps steelorange, gold, green, red, cyan, dimmed, deboss
3Lane notesPer branch: path, ROI, opportunity cost, stop-loss and what it keeps, pre-mortem with falsifierssurface, border
4Cascade rowsExecutive to surgical in one container with hairline dividers, on the --wp-key keyline; the altitude dot and label carry the color (observatory L5 to L1); forks tagged on their altitudegreen, cyan, gold, orange, red
5Fork cardSparkline with keep and kill paths, a keep/kill switch that starts undecided (data decision sets it), keep-if, kill-if, on-ramp, off-ramp, if true, if false, premises with falsifiersgold, green, red

Usage

Use it when

  • A plan has to show, week by week, what must be true for it to work and how it fails gracefully.
  • The reader decides keep or kill at named forks, so the forks, ramps and stop-losses need to be visible before the work starts.

Do not use it when

  • Do not use it for a dated list of deliverables with no forks; that is 46 Day List or 13 90-Day Build.
  • Do not use it to show measured results; that is 07 Probability Bar or 04 Signal Delta Table. This organism draws shape until values are set.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
future_perfect{text, status, source?}yesThe end state, written as done.
weeks[]weekyesA week with draft: true renders as not drafted.
weeks[].cascade{executive..surgical}yesOne claim per altitude.
weeks[].kairos[]{id, day, fork, premises[], keep_if, kill_if, onramp, offramp}yesEach premise carries a falsifier.
weeks[].scenarios{best, base, worst}yesEach with roi, opportunity_cost, stop_loss, p and p_basis; p stays null until set.
weeks[].derisk[]{method, verb, lens, altitude}yesLens keys match the hypercube explorer.
weeks[].orders[]treeyesDepth equals order, first to fifth.
statussourced | hypothesis | confirmedyesOn every leaf; sourced needs a source. Schema: runtime/specs/week-plan.schema.json.

Access

  • Weeks are a real tablist: arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs; without JavaScript every week shows, stacked.
  • Each sparkline has a text title or label; every line it draws is also written out in the lane notes and fork cards, so nothing is carried by color alone.
  • The keep/kill switch is two buttons with aria-pressed; a polite live region says what changed and names the off-ramp.
  • Fog grain never lowers text contrast; print drops the grain and opens every fold and week.
